questions.q: According to this lesson, what should your ServiceNow portfolio be built from?
options: A list of every lesson and topic covered across all thirteen courses
The specific handful of labs and capstones that produced an actual, finished artifact
Only the lessons that included a certification exam objective
A summary of ServiceNow's own marketing materials about the platform
questions.explain: A portfolio needs finished artifacts you can describe and defend, not a syllabus of topics you studied.

questions.q: Which artifact does this lesson identify as the strongest one to lead with in an architecture-level conversation?
options: The Flow Designer automation build from course 4
The REST integration from course 7
The Technical Architecture capstone: the Meridian Health Network enterprise architecture exercise
The ITSM implementation configuration from course 8
questions.explain: The Meridian Health Network capstone demonstrates instance strategy, governance modeling, and ADR writing — exactly what architecture-level conversations test for.

questions.q: What is the honest, accurate way to describe these six portfolio artifacts to an interviewer?
options: As production systems that were deployed to real end users in a live enterprise environment
As self-directed lab or capstone projects built on a Personal Developer Instance to demonstrate applied skill
As work that doesn't matter because it wasn't done for a paying client
As projects that should be described vaguely so the interviewer can't ask follow-up questions
questions.explain: These were built on a free PDI as course exercises — real, demonstrable applied skill, but not production deployments, and the honest framing holds up better under follow-up questions.

questions.q: Why does this lesson warn against overselling these projects as production enterprise deployments?
options: Because the work itself has no value and shouldn't be mentioned at all
Because interviewers never ask follow-up questions about project scope
Because an inflated claim doesn't hold up under follow-up questions the way an honest, accurate description does
Because ServiceNow prohibits discussing Personal Developer Instance work in interviews
questions.explain: Overselling is the easiest way to lose credibility — the honest version of the story is also the more credible one once an interviewer probes for detail.

questions.q: Which two artifacts does this lesson recommend leading with for a Developer-track conversation?
options: The CMDB/CSDM data model and the Meridian Health Network capstone
The ITSM implementation configuration and the Flow Designer automation build
The scoped application with Business Rules/Script Includes and the REST integration
Only the certification exam prep materials from Chapter 1
questions.explain: The scoped application and REST integration demonstrate real server-side code and a real integration pattern — the two things a Developer-track conversation is most likely to probe.
